title: Monthly New Customer Signups
description:
Count how many new customers signed up in each **year-month**, based on `signup_date`. Return year, month, and count.

**Table: customers**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| email | VARCHAR |
| city | VARCHAR |
| country | VARCHAR |
| signup_date | DATE |

Output columns: `signup_year`, `signup_month`, `new_customers`. Order by `signup_year`, `signup_month`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, country VARCHAR, signup_date DATE); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com','New York','USA',DATE '2026-01-10'),(2,'Bob','bob@example.com','London','UK',DATE '2026-01-22'),(3,'Carol','carol@example.com','Chicago','USA',DATE '2026-02-05'),(4,'Dan','dan@example.com','Mumbai','India',DATE '2026-02-18'),(5,'Eve','eve@example.com','Paris','France',DATE '2026-02-28'),(6,'Fay','fay@example.com','Berlin','Germany',DATE '2026-03-14');
solution_sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) AS signup_year, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM signup_date) AS signup_month, COUNT(*) AS new_customers FROM customers GROUP BY signup_year, signup_month ORDER BY signup_year, signup_month
hints: EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) and EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) give the year and month numbers.
GROUP BY both to get one row per year-month bucket.
explanation: Extracting year and month and counting per group gives a monthly growth view. January had 2 signups, February 3, March 1.
